out: Prison Link Cymru is warning that a chronic shortage of suitable housing is leaving many ex-offenders homeless, often leading to a cycle of reoffending. The charity argues that investing in affordable one-bedroom flats would be more cost-effective for the public than the expense of repeated imprisonment. While women often receive more support due to specific needs, men frequently struggle to find priority housing due to issues like PTSD and drug dependency.

Following searches in the Waterfront Park and Colonsay View areas on Wednesday, police recovered three firearms, ammunition, and a large sum of money. A 26-year-old man arrested during the operation appeared in Edinburgh Sheriff Court on Thursday.

Four individuals appeared in a Chicago court facing multiple charges, including hate crimes and kidnapping, for the brutalization of an 18-year-old victim. Prosecutors allege the suspects held the victim captive, physically assaulted him, and targeted him based on his race and disabilities. Due to the severity of the crimes, the judge denied bail for all four suspects.

The former Arsenal goalkeeper and long-time West Brom director of football has left the club. During his tenure, he played a vital role in helping the team achieve two promotions to the Premier League.

A study published in the journal *Cell* suggests that a "fasting-mimicking diet" can reverse diabetes symptoms by regenerating insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas. By cycling between five days of low-calorie eating and 25 days of normal eating, researchers were able to trigger a cellular reprogramming that restored organ function in mice. Experts believe these findings could lead to significant new treatments for both type 1 and type 2 diabetes without the need for genetic alterations.

The proposed merger between lens manufacturer Essilor and frame maker Luxottica aims to create a global eyewear behemoth, though critics warn it could lead to a market stranglehold. While the companies claim the deal will drive innovation, industry experts fear the merger will reduce consumer choice and squeeze out independent competitors.

Olympic silver medallist Joanna Houvenaghel has accused British Cycling of "ageism" and prioritizing medals over athlete welfare following a leaked report detailing the organization's cultural failings. The report suggests that previous investigations into sexism were sanitized, prompting British Cycling to implement a 39-point action plan to address these systemic issues. This comes as part of a broader scrutiny of the "win-at-all-costs" culture within British sport.

After purchasing a struggling Austin comedy club in 2009, Kareem Badr successfully turned the business around by applying his computer science background to its operations. His success reflects a broader national trend as the comedy club industry grows, driven by a new "golden age" of stand-up and shifting audience interests.

BT shares rose after Ofcom decided against breaking up the company, citing practical obstacles such as the complexities of its £40bn pension scheme. Instead of a full split, regulator Sharon White plans to enforce separation by introducing new rules that prioritize customer service alongside shareholder interests. While this avoids an immediate breakup, the new regulations may lead to future legal battles over how much control BT retains over its Openreach infrastructure.

Ahead of the Old Firm derby at Hampden Park, manager Brendan Rodgers expressed confidence in his team's ability to replicate their recent dominant performance. While acknowledging the difficulty of the fixture and past semi-final defeats, Rodgers is focused on maintaining a high level of play to secure his first trophy with Celtic.

In response to an £8m funding cut, Queen's University plans to reduce its undergraduate student intake by over 1,000 places and cut staff positions over the next three years. While there are no immediate plans to close departments, officials warned that the reduction could damage the university's reputation and negatively impact the local economy. Education Minister Stephen Farry expressed concern that these cuts may force students to seek opportunities elsewhere in the UK, potentially harming the regional economy.

An administrative error by an external printing company caused approximately 850 patients to receive incorrect leaflets suggesting they might have cancer. The East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust has apologized for the mistake and is contacting those affected to explain the error.

Despite internal divisions and recent rebellions within the shadow cabinet, Emily Thornberry stated that Labour will not "frustrate Brexit" even if they fail to secure key amendments to the draft legislation. The party aims to amend the bill to ensure a "meaningful vote" on the final deal, while leader Jeremy Corbyn prepares to address disciplinary issues following recent defiance of party orders.

After the transfer of midfielder Lewis O'Kane, former club Torquay United will not be seeking the 15% sell-on clause included in his original sale. Former player Paul Nicholson stated that the cash-strapped club has more pressing priorities than collecting the fee.

An inquest is investigating the death of Iwan Wyn Lewis, who was found dead in the Menai Strait after leaving a psychiatric ward. A consultant psychiatrist testified that a police visit regarding bail arrangements likely caused the 36-year-old significant distress and agitation prior to his death.

After signing a new one-year deal this summer, 33-year-old former Blackpool forward Taylor-Fletcher has only appeared twice for the Foxes this season. He recently joined the 13th-placed Owls prior to their match against Norwich City.

Fearing that the incoming Trump administration may restrict access to climate research, many U.S. scientists are proactively copying federal data to external servers. While some experts argue that maintaining open access to taxpayer-funded data is essential for the public interest, others are taking preemptive measures to prevent the loss of information seen during previous administrations.

The legendary drummer Brad Bradbury, a founding member of the ska group The Specials, has passed away in England. His family and colleagues remembered him as a groundbreaking musician whose powerful drumming was essential to the band's iconic Two Tone sound.

Tiger Woods missed the cut at Torrey Pines after shooting a second-round 72, marking a frustrating return to competitive play following a long injury layoff. Other high-profile players, including Jason Day, Dustin Johnson, and Jimmy Walker, also failed to make the cut. Meanwhile, overnight leader Rose currently holds the lead at eight under par.

Former Manchester United striker Cole has returned to his ambassador role following a kidney transplant from his nephew. While he is making physical progress, he faces a long recovery process and must manage the risks of potential organ rejection.

Pakistan has lifted its long-standing ban on YouTube following an agreement with Google to launch a Pakistan-specific version of the platform. Under this new arrangement, the government can request the removal of offending material, though YouTube maintains that all requests will undergo a thorough review to ensure they meet community guidelines. While many users have welcomed the move, some activists are calling for greater transparency regarding the specific terms of the deal.

Following a recent injury, 26-year-old player Benjamin is expected to be sidelined for the remainder of the season, though director Richard Cockerill noted he is expected to make a full recovery. Meanwhile, 24-year-old scrum-half Sam Harrison has signed a new contract with the team, though its duration remains undisclosed.

Welsh cyclist Owain Doull helped Great Britain win Olympic gold in the team pursuit, setting a new world record in the process. The victory provided personal redemption for Doull after previous silver medals and marked a significant achievement for Welsh cycling.

As floodwaters recede, the death toll has doubled with over 100 bodies discovered, leaving approximately 450,000 people affected in Gujarat. Meanwhile, monsoon rains have caused widespread devastation across 20 Indian states, including the displacement of thousands in Assam. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to visit Assam this Tuesday to discuss permanent solutions to the region's recurring flooding crisis.

Two snowsports enthusiasts, Bridget and Jonathan Reid, celebrated their wedding at the Nevis Range ski resort in Scotland while wearing full wedding attire. The couple chose the location because their first date was a skiing trip, and they celebrated the occasion by sliding down a run together.

The Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission has fined RBS following the conviction of a former trader for falsifying emerging markets trade records. While regulators cited "seriously inadequate" internal controls, they noted that the bank received credit for its prompt cooperation once the illegal activity was discovered.

Following the BAFTA awards, winners shared reflections on their achievements, including Tom Holland discussing the physical toll of playing Spider-Man and Dev Patel celebrating his journey from teen drama to international stardom. The ceremony also featured strong support for Meryl Streep, with Viola Davis and Casey Affleck praising her influential Golden Globes speech and her legendary career.

After a dominant 2016, Andy Murray has struggled with injuries and inconsistent results throughout the early part of 2017. As he prepares for Wimbledon, questions remain regarding how his hip injury and recent losses to lower-ranked players will affect his movement and performance. While his Grand Slam pedigree makes him a formidable contender, his current physical condition and form make his ability to defend his success uncertain.

Mandla Hlatshwayo, a beloved 40-year-old radio DJ, was shot and killed after intervening to stop a group of men from robbing women at a Soweto pub. Police have apprehended suspects found with drugs and an unlicensed firearm, and they are currently investigating potential links to the shooting.

Police are investigating a targeted shooting involving a dark-colored car near two primary schools in Liverpool, though no injuries were reported. While students and staff were ordered to stay indoors as a precaution, school officials confirmed that pupils remained safe and the school day continued as planned.

Entering the final event of the Gotzis Hypo-Meeting, Olympic champion Jessica Ennis-Hill sits in third place with 5,544 points. She remains on track to qualify for both the Rio Olympics and the World Championships, provided she meets her target scoring thresholds in the 800m.

The Manor Formula One team has ceased trading after administrators were unable to find a buyer, resulting in staff redundancies and the team's effective collapse. This failure follows a period of financial instability and a significant loss in prize money, leaving the grid with only 10 teams ahead of the upcoming season. The collapse has prompted calls for a European Commission investigation into the FIA and Formula One Group regarding how prize money is allocated to smaller teams.

The upcoming Stormont election on 2 March features 228 candidates, including 70 women, competing for 90 seats. The DUP is fielding the most candidates with 38, followed by Sinn Féin with 34, while various other parties and 22 independents make up the rest of the field.

In response to a traveler's question about currency fluctuations, an expert suggests that while the pound has fallen due to economic shifts, the upcoming US election could further impact exchange rates. To manage risk, the expert recommends "hedging bets" by buying half the currency now and half later, while advising travelers to use comparison sites rather than expensive airport exchanges.

Nineteen-year-old Newcastle University student Zoe Waters was named the winner of the Alternative Model of the Year competition held in Newcastle. Waters, who expressed shock at her victory, plans to pursue a professional modeling career after embracing her unique personal style.

The National Museum of the Royal Navy is consulting the public on a proposal to move the "Yomper" statue from Eastney to the Portsmouth Historic Dockyard as part of a museum relocation project. While officials argue the move would increase the memorial's visibility to more visitors, local campaigners and the Portsmouth City Council are fighting to keep it at its current site to preserve its historical significance.

A suspect known as BM appeared at the Old Bailey facing charges for allegedly failing to contact a monitoring company and report to a police station. This case is believed to be the first instance of a breach of the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation Measures (TPim). While the defendant was granted unconditional bail, he remains subject to the restrictions imposed by his original order.

Former Sussex seamer Anyon has been appointed as the new head coach of the Sussex women's senior team, a role he takes over from Charlotte Burton. In addition to leading the senior side, he will coach the under-19 and under-21 teams, while Alexia Walker will transition into roles across the senior and youth squads.
After a successful trial with the Shakers, 23-year-old defender Wes Brown has signed with Bury. He is expected to be available for the club's League One season opener against Doncaster this Saturday.

Kenneth Branagh’s live-action *Cinderella* has achieved a successful $70m opening weekend by remaining faithful to the original fairy tale rather than modernizing its setting. While some critics noted the film's traditional romanticism, the cast and director suggest that its classic approach allows for deeper, more universal emotional themes. Lead actress Lily James maintains that while the story is traditional, the character remains a strong heroine driven by her own choices.

Ukraine barred Russian singer Julia Samoilova from participating in the Eurovision Song Contest due to her previous violation of Ukrainian border laws regarding Crimea. While the EBU attempted to resolve the conflict by offering a satellite broadcast option, Russia declined to participate, citing political disagreements. This unprecedented move highlights the growing tension between the two nations and turns the music festival into a geopolitical battleground.

Alex McKechnie, a regular at the Cavern Club, recalls the electric atmosphere of seeing The Beatles perform during their early residency in Liverpool. He describes the band as a charismatic, rebellious force that stood out from their peers through their adventurous musicality and irreverent attitude toward authority. To McKechnie, the group represented a sense of youthful rebellion that made them the epitome of excitement for their growing fanbase.

South Africa is moving toward introducing a national minimum wage to combat poverty and inequality, though critics warn it could lead to higher unemployment. While the ruling party supports the proposal, opposition parties and experts argue the proposed rate is too low to sustain a typical household. The government plans to consult with stakeholders and hopes to implement the new wage within two years.

The death of Ethiopian leader Meles Zenawi has sparked fears of a power struggle that could destabilize the entire Horn of Africa. While he was a formidable strategist who drove significant economic modernization, his legacy remains deeply contested due to his increasingly autocratic rule and failure to address systemic poverty.

Despite heavy rain preventing further play at the MCG, Australia holds a 1-0 lead in the three-Test series after taking key wickets during a shortened day. Jackson Bird and Nathan Lyon led the bowling attack as Australia's bowlers dismantled Pakistan's lineup to end the day's play.

In the Leith Walk by-election, the SNP and Scottish Labour secured the two available seats through the Single Transferable Vote system. The election was held following the resignations of Deidre Brock and Maggie Chapman, resulting in a 25.1% turnout. Additionally, the SNP successfully held the Midlothian West seat in a separate by-election.

Tensions between the U.S. and Russia have escalated over the collapsing Syrian ceasefire, with Washington warning that it may suspend military talks due to ongoing Russian-backed airstrikes in Aleppo. While Russia maintains its support for the Syrian government and urges the U.S. to better distinguish between moderate rebels and terrorists, the U.S. maintains that current bombing efforts undermine the possibility of serious negotiations. As the humanitarian crisis in Aleppo intensifies, both nations are reviewing diplomatic options to address the conflict.

Scarlets players Hooker Hughes and Evans have been selected for the Wales squad ahead of the upcoming Junior World Championship in Manchester. Following a successful Six Nations campaign, the pair will represent Wales in Pool A against Ireland, Georgia, and New Zealand.

The outgoing Obama administration has imposed new sanctions on Russia, accusing the country of interfering in the U.S. election and attempting to destabilize democratic processes. Russian officials have responded with sharp criticism, claiming the sanctions are a vindictive attempt to damage bilateral relations and influence the incoming Trump administration.

Jeremy Corbyn is proposing a complete reversal of current policy by abolishing university tuition fees and reintroducing maintenance grants to ensure education is free for all. This "all-or-nothing" approach aims to appeal to younger voters and eliminate the deterrent of rising student debt, though it faces concerns regarding how it will impact university expansion and government funding.

Following the tragic crash of a vintage jet into traffic on the A27, emergency services have concluded their work at the scene while investigations into the incident continue. Authorities are working to provide answers to the families of the eleven victims, and the Air Accidents Investigation Branch is preparing to interview the pilot. While the road is expected to reopen soon, recovery efforts and land reclamation work will continue at the site.

Top intelligence officials, including NSA Director Dan Coats, declined to discuss private conversations with President Trump during a Senate hearing regarding the Russia investigation. While senators expressed frustration over the lack of transparency, the officials maintained that certain information must remain protected from public testimony. This session served as a precursor to James Comey's appearance, where he is expected to provide more direct insight into his interactions with the president.

A private party hosted by the Obamas on Saturday included a guest list of 500 people, ranging from CEOs to celebrities like Tyler Perry and Angela Bassett. The event featured a performance by Prince and Stevie Wonder, and officials confirmed the party was privately funded.
The provided text is a list of specific road names and their associated towns or villages in Northern Ireland. It does not contain a news article or any narrative information to summarize.

In the BBC series *Doctor in the House*, Dr. Rangan helps Emma Gleeson manage severe anxiety and panic attacks by transitioning her from processed foods to a fresh, nutrient-rich diet. This case highlights growing scientific evidence regarding the link between nutrition and mental health, which is often overlooked in routine medical care. By changing her eating habits, Emma experienced significantly improved moods, fewer panic attacks, and greater emotional resilience.

The Alabama Securities Commission has closed its investigation into whether 88-year-old author Harper Lee was manipulated into publishing her newly discovered manuscript, *Go Set a Watchman*. Investigators concluded that Lee was capable of consenting to the release, satisfying concerns originally raised by her doctor regarding her mental capacity.

The United States has suspended bilateral talks with Russia following intensified airstrikes by Russian and Syrian forces against civilians and critical infrastructure in Aleppo. While Washington accuses Moscow of failing to uphold ceasefire commitments, Russia claims the U.S. is shifting blame for the collapse of the truce. Despite the suspension of these coordination efforts, both nations intend to maintain communication regarding counter-terrorism operations to prevent further clashes.

Sadiq Khan's election as London's first Muslim mayor has drawn international attention, with global leaders and media outlets characterizing the win as a significant moment for diversity and democracy. While some commentators viewed the victory as a rebuke to rising Islamophobia and right-wing politics, others noted the historical context of Muslim leadership in Europe. Ultimately, the election highlighted a contrast between Khan's story of social mobility and the elite background of his rival, Zac Goldsmith.

After a traditional advertisement failed to attract applicants, children at St Paul's in Shipley wrote a viral song to list the qualities they desire in a new vicar. The video gained over 30,000 views and widespread media coverage, ultimately leading to the appointment of Henriette Howarth.

Manchester City midfielder Kevin De Bruyne is expected to be sidelined for approximately 10 weeks following an injury sustained during a recent match. The injury could cause him to miss up to 13 games, including critical fixtures in the Champions League and the Manchester derby.

A 27-year-old Swiss man died following a stabbing and arson attack on a train near Salez, which left five other passengers injured. While two victims remain in serious condition, police state that there is currently no indication of a political or terrorist motive. Investigators believe the attacker acted alone and are currently analyzing forensic evidence from the scene.

A Flybe passenger aircraft narrowly avoided a collision with a drone while approaching Cornwall Airport Newquay, prompting an investigation by police and aviation authorities. Although no collision occurred, officials described the incident as a reckless disregard for public safety and are appealing to the public for information to identify the operator.

The Scottish SPCA rescued a grey seal found tangled in a massive amount of netting at Cruden Bay. After being taken to a rescue centre to be cut free, the healthy seal was successfully released back into the water.

The National Library of Scotland has completed the year-long cataloguing of the extensive archive belonging to the late travel writer and war hero Sir Patrick Leigh Fermor. The collection features significant items such as a 1933 trekking notebook and correspondence from notable figures like Prince Charles and Truman Capote. The library now plans to digitize parts of the archive and host exhibitions to share this colorful history with the public.

Mr. Roache has been elected as the new general secretary of the GMB union, defeating Paul McCarthy with 56.7% of the vote. A veteran with 35 years of experience, Mr. Roache succeeds Paul Kenny and aims to lead the union into the 21st century.

Despite her intense struggles with stage fright and anxiety, singer Laura Mvuzu is preparing for a major career milestone with the release of her second album, *The Dreaming Room*. Ahead of her performance on *Later... with Jools Holland*, she reflects on the excitement and terror of her upcoming live appearances and the importance of the show's supportive environment.

After undergoing surgery and chemotherapy for cancer, Newcastle United player Jonas Gutierrez expressed his emotional relief at returning to professional football. He described the experience as feeling "born again" and is now focused on working hard to secure his place in the Premier League.

Exeter City reported a £1.642m profit for the 2014-15 period, largely driven by the record-breaking £1.75m sale of midfielder Matt Grimes. This financial turnaround follows a period of severe cashflow problems that previously forced the club into an emergency loan and a transfer embargo. The board now plans to use the transfer funds to improve the club's infrastructure and support the redevelopment of St James Park.

Abdullah Hayayei, a veteran UAE para-athlete, tragically passed away after a training cage collapsed on him at the Newham Leisure Centre in London. Police and the Health and Safety Executive are currently investigating the incident, which occurred while Hayayei was preparing for the World Para-athletics Championships. A moment of silence will be held in his honor during the championships' opening ceremony this Friday.

A survey by the Scottish Chambers of Commerce shows growth across several sectors and a positive outlook for 2017, contrasting with more recent weak economic data. While sectors like manufacturing and tourism show signs of recovery, businesses remain wary of challenges such as rising prices, skill shortages, and fluctuating consumer demand. Ultimately, the economic outlook remains finely balanced, with success depending on how firms manage rising costs and shifting trade conditions.

An inquiry has opened in London to investigate allegations of human rights abuses and misconduct involving undercover police officers, including officers entering into deceptive relationships with activists. The proceedings aim to examine whether these tactics resulted in miscarriages of justice and to provide recommendations for future policing practices. Victims and families involved are calling for the full truth to emerge to ensure such abuses never happen again.

In a gritty and physical encounter, the All Blacks secured a narrow two-point victory over South Africa to advance to the World Cup final. Despite falling behind at half-time, decisive plays from Dan Carter and Beauden Barrett allowed New Zealand to overcome the Springboks' ferocious defense. The win positions the defending champions as favorites to retain the trophy in their upcoming semifinal match.

The National Trust is using ground-penetrating radar and sensors to assess the structural integrity of the 1817 Wellington monument in Somerset. This crucial survey aims to identify internal voids and material composition to develop a more effective, sustainable repair approach for the historic tower.

The world's largest clothing retailer, Inditex, reported an 8% increase in net earnings to €1.26bn for the first half of the year, driven by strong sales and international expansion. The group's growth was fueled by significant investments in digital technology and the expansion of its online presence across 40 countries. This strong performance sets the company apart from competitors as it continues to integrate its brick-and-mortar and online retail channels.

Lady Gaga is undergoing intensive rehearsals to prepare a career-spanning performance for the upcoming Super Bowl. The article reflects on the high stakes of the event by revisiting iconic, high-energy moments from past performers like Michael Jackson, Bruce Springsteen, and Beyoncé.

Following the release of the documentary *The Betrayed Girls*, survivors and officials are highlighting ongoing concerns regarding child sexual exploitation in Greater Manchester. While police and local councils state they have learned vital lessons and are committed to preventing such crimes, victims and legal experts warn that many survivors still feel unheard and that current support systems must become more proactive.

A heavy water leak from a rooftop room caused significant damage to stock and a ceiling at the Victoria Centre store on Tuesday night. While staff are working around the clock to clean up, the store will remain closed until further notice.

The FCC has been targeted by a massive influx of over 400,000 automated comments regarding net neutrality, which experts believe were generated by bots using stolen personal data to appear authentic. While some view this surge as a modern form of digital protest, critics warn that the artificial activity could mislead regulators and undermine genuine public opposition.

Following a takeover, Sale Sharks' new director Jason Cotton aims to rebuild the club's reputation and improve the fan experience at the AJ Bell Stadium. To address declining attendances, the club is focusing on infrastructure improvements and increased board involvement to foster a stronger, more competitive presence in the North of England.

Disney's *Moana* achieved the second-highest Thanksgiving debut of all time with an $81.1m opening, despite controversy regarding the appropriation of Pacific Island culture. Other films like *Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them* and *Allied* saw lower box office returns, while Warren Beatty's *Rules Don't Apply* faced a weak debut.

The third seed, world number 18 Naomi Konta, secured a comfortable victory over an American wildcard with a 6-3, 6-1 win. Following her dominant performance, she will face China's Saisai Zheng in the next round on Friday.
Two men were hospitalized for injuries following an attack on Linn Road on Sunday afternoon. Police are currently appealing for anyone with information regarding the incident to come forward.

Researchers investigating the source of an Ebola outbreak in Meliandou believe the virus was transmitted to a young boy through contact with bats in a hollowed tree stump. While the bats were a potential source, scientists noted that the event was likely a rare occurrence and emphasized that culling the animals is not a solution. Instead, the team suggests that understanding how humans and wildlife coexist is vital to preventing future outbreaks.

World number two Shaun Bingham's participation in the upcoming tournament depends on whether his wife gives birth before his first-round match against Joe Perry. While his wife is supportive of him playing, Bingham noted that he will need to consult with her once the baby arrives.

The council has voted to urgently dismantle a dangerous section of a Grade II listed pier to prevent further collapse. The work is expected to take three weeks, with parts of the structure being saved and stored for future use. While up to £650,000 has been allocated, the final cost remains uncertain due to the hazardous nature of the project.

The Campaign to Protect Rural England is launching a High Court challenge against the £21.5m Castle Mill development in Oxford, arguing that the council failed to conduct a necessary environmental impact assessment. While the university plans to occupy the buildings by October, critics argue the development spoils the historic skyline and threatens a protected site. The council has defended the project, noting that the legal challenge was filed after the housing was already built.

The Olympus Trust has warned that severe government funding cuts have pushed its schools to a "crisis point," leading to potential measures such as shortened school days, job cuts, and increased class sizes. While the Department for Education claims new funding plans will increase the trust's budget, unions and parents argue that the proposed changes fail to address the reality of declining spending power. The trust's leadership stated that these "unthinkable" decisions may become necessary by September to manage the financial deficit.

Efforts by developing nations to expand forest reserves to curb carbon emissions risk displacing millions of people, particularly in countries like Liberia and the Democratic Republic of Congo. Experts warn that these conservation efforts often overlook the rights of indigenous communities who have historically protected these lands. Advocates argue that instead of forced displacement, international funding should support local populations whose traditional management often results in higher carbon sequestration.

A human skull and additional skeletal remains were discovered by workers near the M54 slip road close to Telford. West Mercia Police have launched an investigation to identify the adult male and are working with neighboring forces to check missing persons reports. The area remains partially closed as forensic examinations and excavations continue.

In the Olympic boxing finals, 23-year-old Dusmatov secured a unanimous points victory to take the gold. Meanwhile, Colombia's Martinez made history as the nation's first Olympic boxing finalist, while Nico Hernandez and Joahnys Argilagos earned bronze medals.

The University and College Union has rejected a 1.1% pay offer from universities, calling it an "insult" compared to the significant raises received by vice-chancellors. While employers maintain the offer is at the limit of affordability, unions are balloting members on potential strike action for the autumn term. The dispute has already led to staff refusing overtime and extra work as they push for a much-improved deal.

The Scottish government has "called in" a proposal by East Dunbartonshire Council to close St Joseph's Primary in Milngavie to facilitate a merger with a school in Bearsden. The decision follows concerns from ministers regarding allegations of inaccurate information in the council's consultation documents and unresolved issues raised by Education Scotland. While parents and the Catholic Church are fighting the closure, the council maintains the plan is a necessary step to modernize the school estate and address significant budget cuts.

Kazuyoshi Miura, the legendary Japanese striker known as "King Kazu," has signed a contract extension to continue playing professionally past his 49th birthday. His career, which began in Brazil in 1986, spans over 30 years and includes being the oldest scorer in Japanese football history.

Violence erupted in Kashmir as security forces used tear gas to disperse protesters marking the anniversary of militant leader Burhan Wani's death. Meanwhile, shelling across the Line of Control resulted in seven deaths, further escalating tensions between India and Pakistan in the disputed region.

A "Leave" vote in the referendum is expected to cause significant financial instability, particularly regarding bank liquidity and volatile exchange rates. To mitigate these risks, central banks are prepared to provide extra liquidity to banks and use foreign currency reserves to stabilize shifting exchange rates. Existing international swap lines and strategic market interventions serve as key tools to manage these potential economic shocks.

After a successful professional rugby career, 33-year-old back-row forward Dan Easter is retiring from the sport following the conclusion of the season. He will transition into a new career as a teacher at Wrekin College, a move he has been preparing for over the last few years.

An investigation into the closed Tawel Fan ward at Glan Clwyd Hospital has revealed that inadequate medical care may have contributed to the deaths of at least seven patients. While the Betsi Cadwaladr health board is conducting a thorough review to establish the truth, grieving families have expressed frustration over the lack of accountability and unanswered questions. The scandal has left the health board under special measures and continues to face scrutiny as further mortality reports are awaited.

Declan Paul Butcher has been sentenced to 14 months in prison for two "single punch" assaults in Limavady that left two men unconscious and caused serious injury. The court heard that Butcher, a repeat offender with 51 previous convictions, inflicted "gratuitous violence" on innocent victims during the 2014 attacks.

Following a controversial incident involving her husband, US Soccer player Hope Solo has announced she will take a break from the team to decompress. Head coach Jill Ellis stated that Solo's decision was a result of poor judgment that negatively impacts the team, causing her to miss upcoming matches against France and England.

Omar Khan and three others have pleaded guilty to conspiracy to supply cocaine following a case involving the recovery of 1kg of the drug. Khan, a former employee of The Johnson Partnership, was described by his former partner as a hard-working individual who is now facing sentencing on April 15.

The British Transport Police will begin deploying specially trained officers equipped with Tasers across Scotland to combat a "severe" international terrorism threat. This decision brings Scottish rail security in line with English counterparts and provides officers with an additional option to protect the public and themselves. To ensure accountability, all Taser deployments will be subject to strict internal reviews and oversight by the Police Investigations and Review Commissioner.

ID Systems, an industrial utilities company, has secured loan and equity backing from Tata Steel subsidiary UKSE to fund an expansion drive. This investment follows the acquisition of several long-term projects and will allow the company to more than double its workforce across Glasgow and Lanarkshire.

Following the tragic plane crash that killed 71 people, survivors including Chapecoense defender Helio Hermito Zampier Neto are in stable condition after undergoing multiple surgeries. Investigations suggest the aircraft ran out of fuel, as the pilot reportedly proceeded with the flight despite warnings regarding fuel levels. In response to the tragedy, Bolivia has suspended the operating license of the charter airline LaMia while authorities work to determine responsibility for the crash.

A public consultation is underway regarding a proposed tunnel to expand the A303, a plan supported by English Heritage but opposed by anti-tunnel campaigners. Critics, including historian Tim Robinson, argue the project risks damaging the wider archaeological landscape and suggest more comprehensive protection is needed. While Highways England claims the scheme will reduce congestion and enhance the site, the Stonehenge Alliance is calling for more diverse options to be explored.

Everton secured a dominant 4-1 victory over Wolfsburg to move to the top of Group H in their first Europa League appearance since 2010. Goals from an own goal, Seamus Coleman, Leighton Baines, and Kevin Mirallas fueled the win, rewarding manager Roberto Martinez for fielding a strong starting lineup. This impressive attacking performance provides significant momentum as the club aims to progress deep into the tournament.

After making 119 league appearances since joining in 2013, 35-year-old defender Bishop is moving on from his longtime club. Following a season that ended in a disappointing play-off defeat, he expressed a sense of "unfinished business" regarding his departure.
Pawel Sroka, 33, has been charged with the murder of his partner, 29-year-old Joanna Trojniak, following a fatal stabbing. Sroka is scheduled to appear at Bromley Magistrates' Court on April 4.

Despite being a leading cause of cancer death in men, prostate cancer has often been overlooked due to social stigmas and a lack of patient advocacy. To address this, researchers involved in the COGES study have identified 23 new genetic markers associated with the disease, offering hope for better screening and targeted treatments. These discoveries, alongside advancements in precision radiotherapy, aim to improve diagnosis and reduce the side effects of treatment for men worldwide.

Wasps secured a victory and a place in the end-of-season play-offs despite a performance that director of rugby Dai Young described as underwhelming. The match was marked by disciplinary issues, as Bryce Heem was sent off for Worcester and Matt Mullan was sin-binned for Wasps.

Following a deadly terrorist attack at the Bardo museum claimed by Islamic State, Tunisian Prime Minister Habib Essid has dismissed several police chiefs and admitted to security shortcomings. In response to the tragedy, a massive march against terrorism is planned for Sunday in Tunis to honor the victims and support the country's transition.

Satellite imagery reveals that IS militants have systematically destroyed buildings and sabotaged runways at the Mosul airport to prevent advancing Iraqi forces from using it as a logistical base. This scorched-earth tactic, which also clears lines of sight for defensive positions, makes the facility significantly harder to repair than previous sites. The destruction aims to deny the coalition and government forces a vital strategic asset during the ongoing military offensive to reclaim the city.

Major engineering work on the line between Reading and London Paddington is scheduled for the Easter break to address significant bottlenecks and complete station redevelopment. While Network Rail warns of potential delays following previous project overruns, they have prepared hundreds of replacement buses to mitigate passenger disruption.

Natural Resources Wales has approved plans for Coastal Oil and Gas Limited to conduct exploratory drilling at St Nicholas, provided the company adheres to strict environmental protections and avoids fracking. The permit was granted despite a temporary moratorium on fracking in Wales, as officials emphasized that the work must be completed within 12 months and must not harm the environment.

Amazon is shifting its European retail sales registration from Luxembourg to local branches in the UK, Germany, Spain, and Italy. This move follows years of criticism regarding tax avoidance and an ongoing EU investigation into whether such low-tax deals constitute illegal state aid.

Junior doctors in England have begun strike action, limiting their work to emergency care only, following failed negotiations over a new contract and weekend pay. While the BMA maintains the strikes reflect deep-seated professional frustration, Dame Sally Davies warned that the industrial action could lead to patient suffering. Further talks between the BMA and NHS bosses are scheduled to continue next week.

Nineteen-year-old player Kenny has become eligible to compete in the Football League Trophy final against Barnsley this Sunday. Oxford head coach Michael Appleton praised the young talent, noting his bright future and the high regard in which he is held at Goodison Park.

Kingston Maurward College and Weymouth College have been awarded grants to fund significant building and refurbishment projects. These investments are part of a larger £214m national initiative designed to provide first-rate facilities and support high-quality teaching across English colleges.

The family of former footballer Jeff Astle has been invited to Wembley Stadium to meet with FA chairman Greg Dyke to discuss the risks of head injuries in football. The meeting follows a medical determination that Astle died from brain damage caused by heading heavy leather balls rather than Alzheimer's disease. The family is using this platform to campaign for better player education and research into the long-term effects of concussions.

As the global wealth gap reaches its widest point in decades, experts and the wealthy elite are debating the causes and consequences of extreme economic inequality. While some argue that increased awareness of wealth disparity is a natural result of a more connected world, others highlight how the growing gap hinders social mobility for the rest of society.

Eighteen-year-old identical twins have made history as only the fourth set of twins to play side-by-side in the Premiership for Sale Sharks. Both back-row players have impressed in several appearances this season and are seen as key components of the club's academy development vision.

Police are searching for a man in his late teens or early 20s following an incident near Corbett Place and Calais View on Thursday morning. He is described as being approximately 5ft 9in tall with short, dark, curly hair and was wearing a dark top. Authorities are urging anyone with information to get in touch.

Negotiations for a regional nuclear forum proposed by Egypt were blocked by the US, UK, and Canada, preventing a potential forced clarification of Israel's nuclear status. While Western officials accused Arab nations of proposing unworkable conditions, Egypt warned that the failure to reach a deal would have political consequences. As a result of the failed consensus, the next review conference is not expected until 2020.

While the UK government has introduced measures to speed up fracking applications in England, Welsh ministers have reaffirmed a continued ban on the practice to prioritize renewable energy. Natural Resources Minister Carl Sargeant clarified that the new guidance does not lift the moratorium in Wales, where the focus remains on sustainable development. This tension highlights the differing energy policies between the UK government and the Welsh Government.

Since defeating Wladimir Klitschko, Tyson Fury has experienced a volatile period marked by mental health struggles and the relinquishing of his heavyweight titles. The article suggests that reaching the pinnacle of boxing may have caused him to lose focus, mirroring historical patterns of champions who struggle to maintain motivation after a major upset. Ultimately, his erratic behavior and withdrawal from scheduled fights highlight the unpredictable nature of a career defined by extreme highs and lows.

Wasps boss Dai Young expects several of his in-form players to be included in the upcoming England squad selection. With injuries creating a void at open-side flanker, players like Guy Thompson and Sam Jones are being considered alongside rising talents like Will Evans. While Leicester's Richard Cockerill argues that Evans is not yet ready for international rugby, he believes Mike Williams is prepared for the step up to Test level.

The exhibition *From Dark to Light* at The Old Low Light Heritage Centre explores the life and work of North Shields-born artist Victor Noble Rainbird. Featuring many previously unseen pieces, the collection showcases his paintings of the North Sea and local life alongside poignant drawings created during his service in the Great War.

Former Celtic manager Neil Lennon and Scotland assistant Mark McGhee have welcomed Scott Brown's decision to reverse his retirement and rejoin the national squad. Both coaches believe his return will provide a vital boost to leadership and quality ahead of Scotland's upcoming World Cup qualifier against England.

An RSPCA inspector rescued a buzzard in Bethesda after it became stuck in a wire fence while chasing prey. Despite the incident, the bird suffered minimal damage and was released back into the wild immediately.

Thousands of Crown Post Office workers will begin a walkout on December 19, including Christmas Eve, to protest planned branch closures and pension changes. While the Post Office maintains that 97% of branches will remain operational, the union is calling for a pause on privatization to protect the future of the network.

Following the launch of the Ulster Unionist Party's manifesto, Mike Nesbitt defended his comments regarding potential post-election partnerships, stating he would rather work with the SDLP than Sinn Féin. While his remarks caused some internal friction, Nesbitt maintained that his focus remains on challenging the "incompetence and corruption" of the DUP and Sinn Féin. He expressed confidence that voters will prioritize accountability for the Renewable Heat Incentive scandal over the controversy surrounding his comments.

An operation involving Irish police and customs led to the seizure of over 60,000 vials of illegal steroids, growth hormones, and erectile dysfunction pills. Authorities discovered evidence of an illegal manufacturing operation during the raids, which also included searches in Northern Ireland. While a man was initially arrested, he was later released without charge.

Irish Prime Minister Enda Kenny suggested that Brexit could lead to a future referendum on Irish unity, noting that such a poll would depend on clear evidence of public desire. While Sinn Féin welcomed the possibility as an opportunity for unification, unionist leaders dismissed the comments as "mischievous" and unlikely to occur.

Following a 1-0 win over Yeovil, Morecambe has moved to the top of the league after a strong run of three consecutive victories. Manager Jim Bentley praised veteran Kevin Ellison's professionalism and leadership, while cautioning his players to keep their feet on the ground despite their early-season success.

Qatar has rejected a list of 13 conditions imposed by Saudi Arabia and its allies, claiming the demands are an attempt to limit Qatari sovereignty rather than combat terrorism. While U.S. Secretary of State Rex Tillerson urged the nations to lower their rhetoric and engage in dialogue, the blockading countries maintain that the sanctions are necessary to curb extremism. Despite the diplomatic and economic pressure, Qatar has avoided collapse by utilizing alternative trade routes and remains firm in its refusal to meet the ultimatum.

Suspended UKIP figure Ms. Evans has announced she will not run in the upcoming leadership contest, claiming senior party officials used a disciplinary ban to prevent her from competing. Instead, she has endorsed councillor Lisa Duffy, arguing that the party needs a "clean break from the past" to move toward the political centre-ground.

An Uber driver has been identified and reportedly confessed to the rape of a 26-year-old woman after she was taken to a secluded area. This incident follows a series of high-profile sexual violence cases in India that have prompted calls for stricter oversight of ride-sharing services.

Despite their loss to Portugal, Wales' historic Euro 2016 campaign concluded with a sense of pride and a deep bond between the players and their "Red Wall" supporters. After 58 years without a major tournament, the team's success has broken psychological barriers and established them as a new force in international football. The tournament served as a dreamlike achievement for generations of fans, marking a transformative moment for Welsh football.

The latest Scottish Index of Multiple Deprivation (SIMD) reports that several areas, including Ferguslie Park, remain among the most deprived in Scotland. While local council leaders defend their progress against funding cuts, political leaders are debating whether the solution lies in more government intervention or greater devolution of power. The findings highlight deep-seated inequalities across the country, with Glasgow and Edinburgh seeing shifts in their deprivation statistics.

British pair Cassells and Scrimgeour secured their place in the lightweight pairs final after finishing as the fastest qualifiers in their heat. Meanwhile, Irish Olympic silver medallist Paul O'Donovan also advanced to the lightweight single sculls final following a strong late performance in his semi-final.

The 22-year-old former Kilmarnock player has signed a one-year contract to join Scottish Championship side Raith Rovers. He joins teammates Craig Barr and Mark Stewart, both of whom were part of the squad during last season's campaign.

Liverpool secured a 2-1 victory over Swansea City thanks to second-half goals from Roberto Firmino and a James Milner penalty. Despite a spirited first-half lead, Swansea's defeat marks their third successive loss and leaves manager Guidolin's future at the club increasingly uncertain.

The first-ever positive steroid test in Scottish rugby history has raised serious questions about the pressure on players to increase their size and the potential influence of supplement culture. While the player involved claimed he purchased the substances online, the incident highlights a growing concern that the physical demands of modern rugby may be driving athletes toward illegal performance-enhancing drugs.

TRNSMT, Scotland's newest music festival, is set to take place at Glasgow Green with headliners including Radiohead, Kasabian, and Biffy Clyro. Replacing the traditional T in the Park weekend, the event will feature tight security measures and a zero-tolerance policy regarding drugs and intoxication.

North Korea has officially confirmed the restart of its Yongbyon nuclear reactor, a move intended to increase the quality and quantity of its nuclear arsenal. In response, the White House stated that the international community will not accept North Korea as a nuclear state and urged the regime to fulfill its international obligations instead of engaging in provocations.

A 64-year-old man has been arrested following the discovery of human bones during a reopened murder investigation into the 1990 disappearance of Andrew Bedford. Detectives believe Bedford was shot in Ramsey over three decades ago and are now using forensic anthropology and DNA testing to identify the remains.

Millionaire owner Dr. Marwan Koukash is attempting to transform the struggling Salford City Reds into a powerhouse by aggressively recruiting top talent and lobbying to increase the Super League salary cap. His ambitious plans include potential coaching appointment of Brian Noble and signing star players to boost the sport's profile and competitiveness. While his bold moves have generated significant interest, the financial risks and the feasibility of his "dream" remain subjects of debate.

Ireland secured their third consecutive win in Bangkok by defeating Zimbabwe, moving them closer to a spot in next year's World Twenty20. Led by Isobel Joyce's four-wicket haul, Ireland easily chased down a target of 79 to maintain their perfect qualifying record. This victory sets them up for a crucial encounter against Scotland on Thursday to decide the tournament's top seeds.

Colchester Hospital has been rated as inadequate by the Care Quality Commission due to poor leadership and an over-reliance on unsuitable agency staff. The findings have drawn criticism from the family of a patient who died due to agency staff errors in 2009, noting that many of these issues remain unaddressed. In response, the hospital's chief executive stated that while recruitment has increased, reducing dependency on agency workers remains a primary challenge.

British cyclists Mark Cavendish and Becky James delivered strong performances during the opening events of the Olympic track cycling competition. While Cavendish secured a top-ten finish in multiple races, James set a new Olympic record in the women's sprint qualification to advance to the quarter-finals.

The Northern Ireland executive has announced a reallocation of funds that includes an additional £200m for the health sector to address growing demand and issues like bed blocking. Other funding will be directed toward schools, road maintenance, and further education, with much of the budget being repurposed after planned tax credit cuts were reversed. Health Minister Michelle O'Neill plans to decide how the specific health allocations will be distributed within the coming days.

The Winklevoss twins have filed a new lawsuit against Facebook, alleging that the company suppressed crucial evidence during their previous legal battles over the origins of the social media site. This fresh legal action follows the dismissal of their previous appeal regarding a $65 million settlement reached in 2008. Facebook has dismissed the claims as baseless allegations that have already been rejected by the courts.
A teenage pedestrian was struck by a Ford Focus in Thrybergh, Rotherham, on Saturday. The driver was uninjured, and South Yorkshire Police are now appealing for witnesses to come forward.

Harry Pincher was a prolific *Daily Express* defense correspondent known for his ability to secure scoops through high-level contacts and social gatherings. Throughout his career, he utilized lunches and hunting trips to gather intelligence, often operating in environments that were secretly monitored by intelligence agencies. His work frequently involved navigating the intersection of government secrets, political influence, and investigative journalism.

After initially rejecting a move, Stewart has agreed to personal terms and passed his medical to join Birmingham City. The striker, who has already scored six goals this season, could make his debut in Saturday's match against Leeds.

A former soldier in her 20s has accepted a conditional caution for misconduct in a public office following an investigation into corrupt payments to public officials. As part of the agreement, she will make a £40 payment to an armed forces charity to take responsibility for her actions.

The Care Inspectorate has issued low inspection ratings to two care homes in Glasgow and Bargeddie, with Nithsdale House receiving the lowest possible score of one across several categories. Inspectors identified serious concerns regarding medication administration and a failure to address previous requirements for improvement at both facilities. The Care Inspectorate has warned that further action will be taken if significant improvements to resident care and safety are not made.

Police arrested four men in Enfield on Saturday afternoon following reports of a firearm being seen in a vehicle. The suspects were taken into custody after the car was stopped and are currently being held at a north London police station.

A major power outage caused by a substation failure left tens of thousands of properties without electricity across Lancaster and surrounding areas, causing significant disruption to schools, businesses, and local government services. Power was gradually restored throughout the day, and while most facilities have reopened, the cause of the outage remains unknown.

A judge has quashed the decision by former Local Government Secretary Sajiv Javid to block housing developments at the Hatchfield Farm estate in Newmarket. The ruling found the refusal to be "plainly deficient" and inconsistent with national planning policies, meaning the case must now be reconsidered. The decision follows a legal challenge brought by the Earl of Derby and local groups to ensure development is concentrated within the town rather than dispersed into rural parishes.

Following a series of mechanical failures, groundings, and vehicle damage since its May launch, the Cowes chain ferry service will be free of charge until July 2 to allow for feedback and troubleshooting. While council leaders described the launch as frustrating, they maintained that the issues are "teething problems" being addressed through technical fixes and an official audit. Meanwhile, local business owners are expressing significant financial distress and calling for compensation due to the loss of trade.

Tunisian international Sliti has signed a three-year contract with Lille following a season-long loan with the club. Despite his recent international involvement, the 24-year-old has made only five appearances since returning from the 2017 African Cup of Nations.

The provided text describes British astronaut Tim Peake's activities during his six-week space mission. While in orbit, he took time to conduct experiments and speak directly with children to share his experiences.

Martyn Irvine has been named BBC Northern Ireland's Sports Personality of the Year following a historic season that included becoming the first Irish cyclist to win a world track title in 117 years. Despite suffering a fractured hip mid-year, Irvine secured multiple medals and gold finishes across various international competitions. He beat out high-profile nominees, including AP McCoy and Michael Dunlop, to receive this prestigious recognition.

An Italian C-27J aircraft was intercepted by RAF Typhoons and escorted to Prestwick Airport after losing communication with air traffic control. The aircraft landed safely without incident, and while emergency services were deployed as a precaution, airport operations remained largely unaffected. Local police are now leading the investigation into the incident.

Five men were arrested on suspicion of terrorism-related offenses following the discovery of two suspect devices at a business in Birmingham. The intelligence-led investigation involved searches in both Birmingham and Stoke-on-Trent, with magistrates granting police an additional seven days to question the suspects.

The upcoming European football tournament in France features an expanded field of 24 teams, including debutants Wales and Northern Ireland. While hosts France and defending champions Spain are among the favorites, the tournament's new format and the presence of competitive teams like Germany and England make the outcome difficult to predict.

Great Britain's men's basketball team will face Greece in a friendly match at London's Copper Box as they prepare for the upcoming FIBA EuroBasket. This game serves as Britain's final home fixture before they travel to Poland and Turkey for their final warm-up matches and tournament qualifiers.

Despite playing with 13 men for seven minutes, Australia secured a victory over Wales thanks to a heroic defensive effort and five penalties from Bernard Foley. Wales failed to capitalize on their numerical advantage, marking their 11th consecutive defeat against the Wallabies. Both teams now prepare for their respective quarter-final matchups against South Africa and Scotland.

With head coach Gregor Townsend set to replace Vern Cotter at the end of the season, Scotland players are motivated to secure a victory against Ireland in their upcoming Six Nations opener. Despite facing a highly tactical Irish side and an experienced forward pack, the Scottish squad aims to use the coaching transition as emotional incentive to overcome their historical struggles against Ireland.

In a rare interview, retired General David Petraeus characterized the Islamic State as a formidable enemy that requires both military force and political strategy to defeat. He noted that while the fall of Ramadi was a significant setback, the group's success highlights the need to provide political incentives to Sunni Arabs to ensure long-term stability. Ultimately, Petraeus argued that defeating "industrial-strength" extremism requires a synchronized approach where political reform and military action work in tandem.

The City of Edinburgh Council has reported a cyberattack on its website service provider that resulted in the theft of users' email addresses. While council services remained unaffected, officials have warned the public to watch for an increase in spam and phishing attempts. The incident has been reported to the relevant authorities, and extra security measures have been implemented to prevent further issues.

Escalating violence between rebel forces and the Syrian government has threatened the fragile ceasefire and led the Syrian opposition to consider suspending peace talks in Geneva. While rebel groups launched new attacks in response to strikes on residential areas, the opposition expressed frustration over the deteriorating humanitarian situation and potential bias in UN mediation proposals. Despite the tension, UN envoy Staffan de Mistura indicated that the opposition would remain in Geneva for now to continue informal discussions.

To build a sustainable business, Instagram plans to introduce advertisements to its 150 million users within the next few months. This move aims to finally generate profit for the platform, which has struggled to monetize its massive user base since being acquired by Facebook.

The 2016 Hyundai Mercury Prize features a diverse shortlist of nominees, including Radiohead and artists associated with David Bowie's final works. The ceremony will take place on September 15 at the Hammersmith Apollo, where a panel of judges and a public vote will determine the overall winner.

Retired detective Gurpal Virdi has been acquitted of charges dating back to 1986, including indecent assault and misconduct in public office. During his trial, Virdi claimed the prosecution was part of a long-term campaign by the Metropolitan Police to discredit him following his involvement in the Stephen Lawrence inquiry.

Newly re-appointed Preseli Pembrokeshire MP David Cairns argued that the UK should not remain in the EU single market, as both major political parties opposed it during the election. However, several MPs are calling for a more flexible Brexit approach to ensure frictionless trade and achieve cross-party consensus. This debate highlights the pressure on the UK government to balance the mandate to leave the EU with the need to maintain stable trade relations.

Following the unlawful killing verdict in the Hillsborough inquests, Home Secretary Theresa May held private meetings with victims' families to discuss ongoing criminal investigations and the conduct of South Yorkshire Police. The families expressed their support for May's engagement and discussed the proposed "Hillsborough Law," which would mandate greater cooperation from public officials during investigations. Meanwhile, the IPCC is preparing to submit evidence to the Crown Prosecution Service as part of a massive inquiry into alleged police misconduct related to the disaster.

New Crown Prosecution Service guidance states that virtual mobbing and doxxing will be prosecuted with the same severity as offline harassment. While the CPS emphasized that these measures aim to combat abuse rather than stifle free speech, victims of severe online bullying have expressed skepticism regarding the effectiveness of current laws.

Faizan, a young boy from a farming family, was shot in the back of the head by paramilitary soldiers while returning from his Sunday lessons during a parliamentary by-election in Kashmir. He was one of eight people killed during violent protests and stone-pelting incidents that occurred as voters boycotted the polls. The tragedy highlights the intense tension in the region, as the election saw an abysmal 7.1% voter turnout amid local calls for a boycott.

A woman has died following a fatal incident involving a silver Ford Transit truck on Nantlle Road in Talysarn on Friday afternoon. After being airlifted to Ysbyty Gwynedd, the woman passed away, prompting North Wales Police to appeal for witnesses to come forward.

Four companies have submitted bids for the next Wales and Borders rail franchise, with a decision expected in early 2018. The winning bidder will operate under a "not-for-profit model" that caps profits to allow for reinvestment into the rail network and the delivery of the South Wales Metro. The contract aims to modernize public transport through integrated rail and bus services while driving passenger growth across Wales.

After more than three decades, legendary broadcaster Robbie is stepping down as the permanent host of the Scottish dance music show *Take the Floor*. An MBE recipient and champion of the Doric dialect, he plans to hand over the reins to a younger presenter while remaining available for one-off broadcasts.

After Carlisle United's home ground was flooded, the club was permitted to play their upcoming fixtures at neutral venues, including a recent win at Preston. Stanley manager Coleman has criticized this decision, arguing that playing at neutral grounds provides an unfair advantage and shifts the league rules.

Two supporters were discovered during a security sweep at Old Trafford after becoming separated from their group during a stadium tour. While the pair was handed over to the police, no arrests were made, and United officials stated there was no risk to fans attending the upcoming match.

Accrington Stanley secured a dramatic 3-2 victory over higher-league rivals Preston North End in an EFL Cup derby. Despite two late equalizers from Jordan Hugill, a stoppage-time header from Billy Kee clinched the win for the hosts. This victory marks the second consecutive year that Accrington has knocked out higher-league opposition in the competition.

After his tools were mistakenly taken and then returned by a charity shop in Cardiff, Andrew Bickel’s story went viral, leading to various media offers. Bickel plans to donate any money earned from his "five minutes of fame" to animal charities. He expressed relief that the misunderstanding resulted in no financial loss for anyone involved.

Middle-distance runner Anoudia Muir has announced she will miss next year's Commonwealth Games to focus on completing her veterinary medicine degree. While she is disappointed to miss the opportunity to represent Scotland, she remains optimistic about her future athletic career and is targeting the World Indoor Championships in March.

Former Newcastle striker Nile Ranger is expected to return to training following an eight-month prison sentence for online banking fraud. Southend manager Phil Brown noted that while the player aims to be fit for the season opener, his future with the club remains under consideration.

Veteran broadcaster Sir Terry Wogan has died at the age of 77 following a brave battle with cancer. Tributes from colleagues, politicians, and fans have poured in, celebrating his legendary 50-year career and his ability to make millions of listeners laugh.

Unions at BAE Systems have warned that potential delays to the Royal Navy's new frigate program could threaten up to 800 jobs at Scottish shipyards. While political leaders expressed grave concern over broken promises and job security, Scottish Conservative leader Ruth Davidson insisted that the government's original production timetable remains unchanged. BAE Systems stated they are working with the Ministry of Defence to finalize a revised production schedule and baseline for the vessels.

During a heated Republican debate, Senators Marco Rubio and Ted Cruz launched aggressive personal attacks against front-runner Donald Trump, questioning his business record and conservative credentials. Despite being forced onto the defensive, Trump remained defiant as his opponents attempted to stall his momentum ahead of Super Tuesday.

Ukraine's Jamala secured a surprise victory at the Eurovision Song Contest with her song "1944," a historical piece regarding the deportation of Crimean Tatars. While some experts criticized the win as a political statement against Russia, others noted that the song's focus on historical fact allowed it to bypass rules against current political messaging. The result sparked debate among fans regarding whether the contest was decided by musical quality or political sentiment.

Rother District Council has allocated £51,000 to fund lifeguard patrols at Camber Sands following a series of tragic drownings last summer. The decision aims to protect the public and support the local tourism economy after several unprecedented deaths prompted calls for increased safety measures. While the council is investing in these patrols, officials also emphasized the importance of visitors being well-informed about water safety risks.

Partick Thistle players are expressing their desire for manager Tommy Archibald to stay with the club despite interest from other teams. Both captain Osman and midfielder Adam Barton praised Archibald's leadership and impact on the squad, noting how difficult his departure would be.

Ten individuals were detained at Montreal's Trudeau International Airport over the weekend and had their passports confiscated as part of an ongoing investigation. While no charges have been filed, Public Safety Minister Steven Blaney commended officers for their vigilance against global terror threats.

After making his professional debut for the Tigers in August, 21-year-old former under-21 captain Dixon is set to join the Minstermen. He could make his debut for the bottom-of-the-league club this Saturday in their match against Newport.

The UK government is proposing new measures to save £500 million annually by tackling "health tourism" and recovering costs from foreign visitors to the NHS. While Health Secretary Jeremy Hunt argues these changes will fund 4,000 extra doctors, critics and medical professionals have raised concerns regarding the accuracy of the data and the potential burden on GPs. The proposed plan includes a levy on non-European temporary residents but maintains that emergency care will remain available to everyone regardless of nationality.

The Belfast Giants secured a dominant victory over the Devils with a 5-1 win, fueled by goals from Ryan Martinelli, Mark Garside, Alex Foster, and Steve Saviano. This win keeps the Giants in a strong position as they head into a busy festive schedule. The team now prepares to face the Manchester Storm on Wednesday before continuing their matches against Braehead and Coventry.

After undergoing significant restoration, a historic steam engine is set to make its first journey along the East Coast mainline in ten years. Originally built in Doncaster, this iconic piece of British engineering has toured the world since its original class was withdrawn in 1966.

One of 249 men is seeking compensation from the Catholic Church following historical sexual abuse at St William's residential school. While the De La Salle Brothers have issued an unreserved apology, only one claimant has successfully been awarded damages so far in the High Court.
